tagline: Cool, high-altitude capital with a graffiti-covered old town
summary: Colombia's 2,640 m capital is a sprawling city of museums, street art and food, and Dec to Jan are its driest, sunniest months. Expect cool nights (6 to 8 C) and an urban, big-city pace rather than a beach vibe.
things_to_do: La Candelaria old town and street art

tagline: City of eternal spring with a reinvented, creative core
summary: Warm valley city (about 22 C all year) known for its metro cable cars, Botero sculptures and a big backpacker and nomad scene around El Poblado. Dec brings the Alumbrados Christmas lights across the city.
things_to_do: Botero Plaza and Museum of Antioquia

tagline: Salsa capital of the world, hot and unpolished
summary: Large, hot valley city (about 1,000 m, 24 C average) where salsa clubs and dance schools are the main draw, with far fewer foreign tourists than Medellin or Cartagena. The Cali Fair runs 25 to 30 Dec with concerts and salsa shows.
things_to_do: Cerro de las Tres Cruces hike

tagline: Walled UNESCO colonial city on the Caribbean
summary: Pastel colonial streets inside 16th century walls, a hip Getsemani quarter and boat trips to the Rosario Islands; very hot and humid but Dec to Apr is the dry season. The most touristy stop in the country, with prices to match.
things_to_do: Walled City walk and Plaza de Bolivar

tagline: Caribbean port town and gateway to Tayrona, Minca and Palomino
summary: Colombia's oldest surviving city is a hot, gritty bay town best used as a base for the Sierra Nevada coast. Dry season runs Dec to Apr, so beach and trekking weather is good.

tagline: Coffee Axis transport hub with an airport
summary: Largest city in the coffee region and the usual gateway to Salento, Manizales and Armenia, with a busy bus terminal and Matecana airport. Little reason to stay beyond a night, though the Megacable gondola and Lake Otun are options.
things_to_do: Gateway to Salento and Cocora Valley (about 45 min)

tagline: Caribbean island of seven shades of blue, far off the mainland
summary: Duty-free island 700 km from the mainland with a crowded main beach strip, reef snorkelling and golf-cart touring; English-based Creole culture gives it a different feel from the rest of Colombia. Busy at New Year and on weekends, quieter in the villages like San Luis.

tagline: Quiet, hilly Creole island for diving and slow days
summary: About 5,000 residents, English-Creole speaking, with a Rastafari and Raizal heritage, and a UNESCO Seaflower reserve around it. Rebuilt after Hurricane Iota (2020), mostly small guesthouses and cabanas.
things_to_do: Scuba and snorkelling in Seaflower reserve

tagline: Colourful coffee-region village at the gate of Cocora Valley
summary: A pretty bahareque village of balconies and craft shops, famous for the 60 m wax palms of the Cocora Valley a jeep ride away. Packed at weekends and holidays, calm mid-week.
things_to_do: Valle de Cocora wax palm hike
Coffee farm tour (e.g. Don Elias, Finca el Ocaso)
Trout and patacon on the plaza

hostels.name: Posada Aguanile Finca La Diana
hostels.note: Hostelz FAQ average for Salento: dorm about $14, private about $40

notes: Coffee farm names from general knowledge.

tagline: High-altitude coffee city and university town under a volcano
summary: Steep, cool, spring-like city at about 2,150 m with 30,000 students and the closest base for Nevado del Ruiz and hot springs. Far fewer foreign tourists than Salento. Not usually on the gringo trail.

tagline: Painted lakeside town below El Penol rock
summary: Technicolour zocalo-tiled houses on a man-made reservoir, 2 hours from Medellin and swamped by day-trippers at weekends. Staying overnight gives you the calm evenings and quiet mornings.
things_to_do: Zocalo streets and Plaza de Zocalos
Kayak or paddleboard on the lake

tagline: Jungle-and-beach national park on the Caribbean coast
summary: Coastal rainforest park with white beaches reached on foot or horse, hammock camping at Cabo San Juan and strong currents on most beaches. Typically closes about 1 to 15 February for indigenous rest, so check dates against your itinerary.
things_to_do: Hike to Cabo San Juan beach
Hammock night at Cabo San Juan

hostels.name: Cabo San Juan hammock (in park)
hostels.note: COP 40,000 to 50,000 per hammock per night; DKK not converted (no COP rate given)

notes: 2025 article lists park closures 1 to 15 Feb, 1 to 15 Jun, 19 Oct to 2 Nov; confirm 2027 dates with Parques Nacionales.

tagline: Barefoot beach village where the river meets the sea
summary: Laid-back strip of hostels, hammocks and dirt roads between the Sierra Nevada and the Caribbean, with a wide windy beach and river tubing. Backpacker-friendly and growing quickly.

tagline: Cool mountain hamlet above Santa Marta with jungle ecolodges
summary: Small Sierra Nevada village at about 600 m, popular for waterfalls, coffee farms, birdwatching and sunset viewpoints, and 20 degrees cooler than the coast at night. Most travellers stay in ecolodges outside the village.

tagline: Hot industrial port city, home of Colombia's biggest Carnival
summary: Fourth biggest city (1.3 million), relaxed Caribbean pace, Art Deco and Magdalena riverfront; mostly a transit stop but the Carnival is a big draw. Carnival 2027 is expected around 6 to 9 Feb (Saturday to Tuesday before Ash Wednesday, 10 Feb), confirm locally.
notes: Carnival date is derived from Ash Wednesday 10 Feb 2027, not from a source.

tagline: Adventure capital of Colombia in the Santander hills
summary: Small market town packed with outfitters for rafting, paragliding over Chicamocha canyon, canyoning and caving, with cheap hostels and a young crowd. Barichara, a preserved white colonial village, is 45 minutes away and quieter.
things_to_do: White water rafting on the Suarez or Fonce
Barichara and the Camino Real to Guane

tagline: Whitewashed colonial town with the largest plaza in Colombia
summary: Cobbled streets, 16th century buildings and a 14,000 sqm plaza, three hours from Bogota and very busy at weekends and holidays. Dry desert-like valley with fossils, wineries and cloud forest nearby.
things_to_do: Pozos Azules and Iguaque National Park
notes: Hostelz general estimate: dorm about $5, private about $12 (looks low).

tagline: Gulf of Uraba port town where boats leave for Capurgana
summary: Afro-Colombian beach town, mainly a staging point for boats to Capurgana and Acandi; hot and basic. Also used as a transit point for Darien migrants.
things_to_do: Boat launches to Capurgana and Acandi
notes: Hostelz prices are listing 'from' rates, no date shown.

tagline: Tiny car-free bay village on the Panama border
summary: About 270 residents on a sheltered bay, no roads and no ATMs, with jungle trails to Panama's La Miel beach. Reach by boat from Capurgana (COP 10,000 per sygic guide).
things_to_do: Walk to Playa Blanca and La Miel (Panama)
Hike over the hill to Capurgana (about 1.5 h)
Cabo Tiburon, border of South and Central America
notes: No hostel prices found in allowed sources. Accommodation is cabanas, rooms, hammocks and camping. Bring cash, no ATMs.

tagline: Panamanian border post and airstrip on the Guna Yala coast
summary: Remote settlement of about 670 people with customs and immigration, no roads, only boats and a small airstrip. A functional crossing, not a place to stay.
things_to_do: Boat to or from Sapzurro (about 45 min)
notes: No hostel data found. Sygic guide quotes US$15 launch from Puerto Obaldia to Sapzurro.
